quarterly_data.signal: CFO: 'acceleration' quarter — for the FIRST TIME a Q1 grew sequentially over the record Q4 (historically Q1 was lighter). Cloud infrastructure $7.4B, +121% after Q4's +93%, as record megawatt capacity came online; CFO expects the acceleration to CONTINUE through the rest of FY2027 as more RPO converts. SaaS +10% with Fusion +14% and industry apps >20%; Oracle Health accelerating; NetSuite slower. Non-GAAP operating income $8.2B (+31%); gross margin declined as expected (data-center ramp + infra mix) but was offset by lower operating costs, so non-GAAP operating margin stayed ~flat at 42%. Non-GAAP EPS $1.92 (+30%). Trailing-12-month operating income growth accelerated from 16% (Q4) to 21% (Q1).
quarterly_data.figure: OCI $7.4B (+121%, Q4 +93%); non-GAAP operating income $8.2B (+31%); operating margin 42%; EPS $1.92 (+30%); Fusion +14%, industry apps >20%

quarterly_data.signal: RPO grew $26B from Q4. The vast majority of the new contracts are PREPAY, BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARDWARE or similar mechanics that need no incremental capital from Oracle, and the new RPO will not hit capex or revenue until fiscal 2028 or beyond. RPO is now converting strongly into revenue — Oracle expects around HALF of RPO to convert into sales over the next 36 months. Clay Magouyrk: it still needs capex, just not Oracle's cash — three funding models: (1) supplier financing arrangements that let Oracle pay for capacity as customers pay it, (2) the customer pays for the hardware and Oracle operates it as an AI cluster in its data centers, (3) the customer prepays. Demand for these models is broad-based, from startups to the most valuable investment-grade companies.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO +$26B vs Q4; ~half of RPO converts to revenue over the next 36 months; new RPO affects capex/revenue in fiscal 2028 or beyond

quarterly_data.signal: Cash and capex: record operating cash flow of $23B, including collected customer prepayments. Capex was $28B, so free cash flow was -$5B; net cash capex (after prepayments) was $18B. Capex will not be linear through the year. FY2027 guide reiterated: $90B-$95B capex with not more than $70B net cash capex. The $20B at-the-market equity issuance was completed in full during Q1. No timeframe given for positive FCF, but each project throws off a free-cash-flow conversion of something like 100% of post-tax EBITDA shortly after it ramps.
quarterly_data.figure: operating cash flow $23B; capex $28B; FCF -$5B; net cash capex $18B; FY2027 capex $90B-$95B (net cash capex not more than $70B); $20B ATM completed

capex.period: FY2027 plan (net cash capex not more than $70B)

quarterly_data.signal: Fleet economics: GPU utilization 97.9% (Q4: 97.5%). Of all GPUs up for renewal in Q1, the capacity was renewed or resold at a 20% PREMIUM to prior contracts — and the majority of those GPUs are four years or older ('long, useful life with increasing value'). Q1 delivery was almost three times all of Q4 and 73% of the total capacity delivered in FY2026. ABILENE: 131,000 GPUs delivered in Q1 (1.9x Q4); six of the eight campus buildings (618 MW, 75% of total capacity) now delivered to the customer; customer acceptance compressed to only 24 hours. SHACKELFORD is the next gigawatt-scale campus and is progressing well.
quarterly_data.figure: GPU utilization 97.9%; renewals at 20% premium; Abilene 131,000 GPUs in Q1 (1.9x Q4), 618 MW = 6 of 8 buildings (75%); Q1 delivery 73% of FY2026 total

quarterly_data.signal: Sites and constraints (Q&A): New Mexico and Wisconsin are ~1 gigawatt each; neither Shackelford, New Mexico, Wisconsin nor Michigan contributed to Q1's 850 MW, and large sites phase in over many quarters. NEW MEXICO: data-center construction on track; Oracle is going through the AIR PERMIT process for on-site Bloom fuel-cell generation (Doña Ana County). WISCONSIN: no on-site generation — power delivered through the grid, working with the Public Service Commission, ATC and We Energies; data-center delivery on track. Neither site affects FY2027 revenue or earnings guidance. Binding constraint has moved over time from GPUs and fabs, to power generation, to data centers. Component prices: 'in a world where demand exceeds supply, prices don't go down, they go up' — Oracle charges more to be compensated and does NOT expect an impact on gross margins; prior OCI gross-margin framework still holds.
quarterly_data.figure: New Mexico and Wisconsin ~1 GW each; no impact on FY2027 revenue/EPS guidance; component price increases passed through, no gross margin impact expected

quarterly_data.signal: Database, multicloud and models: multicloud database revenue +353% YoY and multicloud customers +180%. Completed the planned Azure and AWS regional footprint expansion — 70 multicloud database regions and 119 availability zones. Oracle Interconnect for AWS is generally available, so OCI now has private high-speed links to ALL hyperscalers with no data-transfer charges. Model ecosystem: expanded OpenAI relationship (OpenAI API, ChatGPT for work and Codex via Oracle Marketplace, incl. GPT-6 Astra); Gemini models coming to Oracle enterprise apps; new Grok reasoning/multimodal/text-to-speech models; open-source catalog adds models from NVIDIA, Qwen, Google, DeepSeek. Multi-year partnership with Quantinuum to offer its Helios quantum computer through OCI from a US-based OCI AI data center. Sovereign cloud (Alloy) growing with partners in Japan and the Middle East, including GPU capacity for sovereign workloads; general-purpose cloud also growing rapidly with less capital intensity than AI clusters.
quarterly_data.figure: multicloud database revenue +353%, customers +180%; 70 multicloud database regions, 119 availability zones

quarterly_data.signal: Applications AI usage: embedded AI used more than 150 million times in Q1 (+42% QoQ); AI agents executed more than 3.5 million times in production (nearly doubling QoQ); over 2,300 AI agents in production (+90% QoQ); Fusion AI production usage consumed 900 billion tokens in the quarter. NetSuite Next (agentic) generally available; NetSuite AI Connector Service (connects to ChatGPT and Claude) already used by more than 10,000 customers. AI-assisted go-lives cut complex Oracle Health implementations from high double-digit months to single months and NetSuite from double-digit months to single-digit weeks; a new agentic AI implementation accelerator will be unveiled at AI World in October.
quarterly_data.figure: 150M+ embedded AI uses (+42% QoQ); 3.5M+ agent executions; 2,300+ agents in production (+90% QoQ); 900B Fusion tokens; NetSuite AI Connector 10,000+ customers
